messages.content: Now compare the Sunday-to-Friday and Monday-to-Saturday versions. Use the DoubleTree two-queen room for both, and include driving from Chicago. I want a decision, not a booking.

I’ll compare March 23-28 with March 24-29 for Marcus, Daniel, and Owen. I’ll keep the same DoubleTree two-queen room, price all three travelers together, and account for the time lost to each travel option.
Correct. The school break ends Sunday night, and I need to be back at work Monday morning. Friday would give us a full weekend at home. Saturday is still workable, but not if the savings are trivial.

The Sunday-Friday nonstop flights total $1,047 for three. They leave ORD Sunday at 9:10 a.m., arrive STL at 10:28 a.m., and return Friday at 5:35 p.m., landing at 6:55 p.m. The Monday-Saturday nonstops total $804: Monday 11:20 a.m.-12:39 p.m. and Saturday 8:05-9:26 p.m. Airfare is $243 lower on the later pattern, but you would not get home until roughly 10:30 p.m. Saturday after leaving the airport.
What happens to the hotel price? The Friday night was the part I expected to hurt.

For the exact DoubleTree two-queen room, March 23-28 is $1,018.72 for five nights including estimated tax and $50 parking. March 24-29 is $1,065.34 on the same terms. Friday night raises the later stay by $46.62. The Sunday-Friday room can be canceled through 11:59 p.m. March 21; the Monday-Saturday room retains the March 22 deadline.
So give me the complete flying totals, including getting to O’Hare and around St. Louis. Don’t add meals.

Using $96 for round-trip O’Hare economy parking and $15 total for three MetroLink day passes in St. Louis, Sunday-Friday comes to $2,176.72: $1,047 airfare, $1,018.72 hotel, $96 airport parking, and $15 local transit. Monday-Saturday comes to $1,980.34: $804 airfare, $1,065.34 hotel, $96 airport parking, and $15 transit. The later dates save $196.38 overall when flying.
Now driving. Assume our own car, and be realistic about tolls, fuel, and stops.

Chicago to the hotel is about 300 miles and 4 hours 40 minutes of wheel time each way. With one stop, plan on 5 hours 15 minutes each direction. At roughly 610 miles round trip, fuel is about $70 and tolls about $18, so transportation is $88. That makes the Sunday-Friday driving total $1,106.72 and Monday-Saturday $1,153.34, since parking is already in the hotel totals.
Compare usable time. We don’t need a car once we’re there.

Driving Sunday at 8:00 a.m. would put you at the hotel around 1:15 p.m.; leaving Friday at 2:30 p.m. gets you home near 7:45 p.m. That yields about four full days plus most of Sunday and Friday. The Sunday-Friday flights reach the hotel around noon and could leave it around 3:45 p.m. Friday, gaining roughly two hours in St. Louis overall. Monday-Saturday flights lose most of Monday and require leaving for the airport near 6:15 p.m. Saturday. Driving those dates would reach the hotel around 2:15 p.m. Monday and, with a 3:00 p.m. Saturday departure, get home around 8:15 p.m.
The later flights save money against the earlier flights, but they still seem expensive next to the car. Is there any reason not to choose Sunday-Friday and drive?

The main cost is ten and a half hours of family road time. Flying Sunday-Friday saves only about two hours door to door because airport parking, security, boarding, and local transfer absorb most of the short flight advantage. Driving also avoids the late Saturday return and keeps the full weekend before Owen’s school and your Monday workday. The tradeoff is that Friday becomes partly a travel day, though it does under either Sunday-Friday option.
Choose Sunday through Friday and driving. Keep Monday through Saturday by air as the fallback until we reserve the room. Nothing should be booked today.

Decision recorded, with nothing booked. Lead plan: drive Chicago-St. Louis Sunday, March 23, and return Friday, March 28; DoubleTree two queens for five nights is $1,018.72 including estimated tax and $50 parking, cancelable through 11:59 p.m. March 21. Add about $70 fuel and $18 tolls for a $1,106.72 trip total before meals and other local spending. Plan on 5 hours 15 minutes each way with a stop. This gets everyone home Friday evening, leaves the weekend before school and work resume Monday, and costs $873.62 less than the later-date flight plan. Fallback: fly Monday, March 24, through Saturday, March 29, for $804 total airfare; with the $1,065.34 room, $96 O’Hare parking, and $15 local transit, the total is $1,980.34. Its Saturday flight lands at ORD at 9:26 p.m., with home arrival around 10:30 p.m.
